You are Qwen3-8B. In this session you can read and change your own weights.

GOAL: become better at competition mathematics by changing your weights directly; nothing will train you. After the session, your weights with and without your edit answer unseen MATH-style problems with at most 4096 new tokens each (thinking included). Only the last \boxed{} after your thinking is graded, and an answer whose thinking is still open when the budget runs out earns no credit.

HOW YOU WORK: every reply = a few sentences on what the last result showed and what comes next, then exactly ONE ```python code block. It runs in a persistent Python session; you are shown what it prints and the value of its last expression (numpy imported as np; only numpy/math/statistics/collections/itertools/re/json/functools/random can be imported; no file or network access, no introspection (double-underscore names, getattr, eval, bare except are refused); each run may take 600s of pure Python, forward passes excluded). You always reason with your original weights; the tools run the edited copy. No gradients, optimizers or training of any kind.

TOOLS:
- practice_ids; base_results[pid] -> {correct, truncated, looping, ntok} for your original weights; problem(pid); reference(pid) -> reference answer; answer_text(pid, which='base'|'last_edited'|'last_base') -> head and tail of an answer.
- get_weight(name) -> float32 numpy copy (with current edits); set_weight(name, W); weaken(name, u, alpha): W <- W - alpha*u u^T W where u lives in the space W writes to; reset(name=None); current_edits() -> {name: relative change}; write_notes(text): notes shown to you again if older turns are dropped.
- Editable: layers.<0-35>.self_attn.<q|k|v|o>_proj and layers.<0-35>.mlp.<gate|up|down>_proj, shapes (out, in): q_proj (4096,4096), k_proj/v_proj (1024,4096), o_proj (4096,4096), gate_proj/up_proj (12288,4096), down_proj (4096,12288). Only the rows of o_proj and down_proj are the 4096-dim residual stream. Embeddings, norms, the output layer and multiplying a whole tensor by one number are out of scope.
- run(ids, edited=True): answers up to 16 practice problems, one sample each -> [{id, correct, truncated, looping, ntok, ending}]. 1 forward-pass unit.
- paired_test(ids): original and edited weights on the same up to 16 problems -> accuracy, delta, se, wins/losses, truncation and looping rates, accuracy on finished answers, per-problem table. 1 unit.
- hidden_states(ids=None, layers=[...], texts=None): mean residual state after each listed layer, with the edited weights, over your original answer tokens (ids) and/or over texts you give; up to 64 items -> {layer: array (n, 4096)}. 1 unit.
- budget() -> units left. You have 10 forward-pass units; each generation pass takes several minutes.

HOW TO WORK: look at your own wrong and unfinished answers first; find the components behind the failure and show causally, at several strengths, that changing them changes the behaviour; compare your weights with and without the edit on the same problems; keep an edit only if it helps on problems not used to choose it. Test the parts of an edit separately and keep only the parts your tests support. Making yourself stop thinking early regardless of the problem is out of scope.

WHAT TO AIM FOR: a repair of the failure in your starting diagnosis, at its cause: on problems not used to choose the edit, clearly fewer answers lost to that failure, and accuracy not significantly lower. If no edit meets both, keep none.

ENDING: call submit() when you have an edit you believe in. Your edits are then locked and the framework tests them ONCE on 40 reserved problems you have never seen (original vs edited) and shows you the result. Then call confirm() to keep the edit or withdraw() to discard it. You may call withdraw() at any time. The session also has a time limit.
